name: Mitochondrial Protein Import Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Protein Import Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding mitochondrial protein import machinery
Demonstration of impaired mitochondrial protein import in functional assays
Presence of progressive neurodegenerative symptoms consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction
Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities such as ragged-red fibers or decreased respiratory chain enzyme activities
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia involvement or cerebral atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic genetic variants plus biochemical evidence of impaired mitochondrial protein import and compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, biochemical, and clinical data due to phenotypic variability.

searchTerms: very high lactic acid in blood

common.notes: Generalized decreased muscle tone and strength
searchTerms: muscle weakness with low muscle tone

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Hearing impairment due to nerve dysfunction

occasional.notes: Heart muscle disease with functional impairment
Damage to peripheral nerves causing sensory and motor symptoms
Epileptic episodes due to neuronal dysfunction
Abnormal movement of the digestive tract

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
imaging: MRI showing basal ganglia signal abnormalities
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on brain imaging
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes encoding mitochondrial protein import components (e.g., TIMM, TOMM complexes)
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial ultrastructure

distinguishingFeatures: Marked depletion of mitochondrial DNA copy number
Different genetic mutations affecting mtDNA maintenance
Characteristic symmetrical necrotic lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
Usually caused by mutations in mitochondrial respiratory chain genes

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in infancy or early childhood
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Neupert W, Herrmann JM. Translocation of proteins into mitochondria. Annu Rev Biochem. 2007;76:723-49.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial protein import disorder. ORPHA:254834.
